subject: MSA/Order Form — Novaforge: output ownership, training carveouts & feedback license
messages:
From: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.com>
To: Sam Park <sam.park@novaforge.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-21T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: MSA/Order Form — Novaforge: output ownership, training carveouts & feedback license

Hi Sam — attaching our first-pass redline for the MSA + Order Form (see attachment). High-level ask: we want to get to an execution-ready draft that preserves Novaforge's output ownership while giving Redwood limited, well-scoped rights to use telemetry/feedback for product improvement. Key points in the redline: 

- Output ownership: Customer retains ownership of generated output; Redwood will not assert ownership.
- Feedback license: propose a perpetual, non-exclusive, royalty-free license to use CUSTOMER FEEDBACK (as defined) for product/quality improvements and metrics; exclude Customer PII and customer confidential code.
- Training/data use: Redwood will not use raw customer prompts/content for model retraining without explicit opt-in; we propose an opt-in checkbox/annex on the Order Form for training.
- Telemetry: allow collection of non-content telemetry (latency, token counts, error rates) by default; content collection only with consent and further safeguards (masking, aggregation).
- Rollback/fallback: if Novaforge requires, we can offer a one-way training opt-out and provide a tighter definition of "Feedback" limited to metadata and aggregated signals.

Can you confirm whether Novaforge legal needs a narrower definition of "Feedback" (e.g., remove any wording that could be used for model retraining) or whether they're okay with a license scoped to product improvement (not model retrain)? If Novaforge prefers a separate training opt-in annex, we're happy to make that explicit in the Order Form.

Attached: Novaforge_OrderForm_MSARedline_v1.docx 
Drive: https://drive.google.com/novaforge-drafts/Redline_v1

Would like to get legal alignment this week so we can keep the PO timeline. Proposed next step: Novaforge legal marks up our redline and we reconcile.

Thanks —
Alex Martinez
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference

From: Sam Park <sam.park@novaforge.com>
To: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.com>
Cc: Novaforge Legal <contracts@novaforge.com>
Date: 2027-04-21T13:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: MSA/Order Form — Novaforge: output ownership, training carveouts & feedback license

Alex — thanks for the redline and summary. Quick reactions from our side:

- Output ownership: happy that Redwood isn't asking for assignment of output.
- Feedback license: we need this to be much narrower. Novaforge is comfortable with a license to use anonymized feedback for bug fixes and product metrics, but not for model retraining or commercial re-use.
- Training & opt-in: we agree that training should be opt-in. If Redwood needs training data for model improvements, Novaforge will consider a separate commercial arrangement.
- Telemetry: agree to network/latency/usage metrics being collected; anything that includes actual prompt/response content must be consented to and require guaranteed de-identification with examples.

I attached our high-level comments as PDF (redlines inline). Two asks for clarity: (1) please define "anonymized" and give an example of the sanitization/aggregation steps used; (2) confirm whether the feedback license is perpetual and whether it survives termination.

We want to avoid any language that could be read as a general training license. If Redwood can produce a short compromise paragraph that restricts usage to internal product improvement (no model retrain / no commercial derivative products) we can take that to our CISO/legal for a quick review.

Thanks,
Sam Park
Head of Cloud Partnerships, Novaforge

From: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.com>

Laura/Jordan — forwarding Novaforge's reply (below). They pushed back on any language that could be used for model retraining and want a tight definition of "anonymized" plus confirmation the license survives termination. Deal team notes / proposed options: 

Options to propose back:
- Option A (preferred): Keep feedback license but explicitly carve out model retrain; preserve perpetual license for product improvement (bug fixes, telemetry, internal metrics).
- Option B (compromise): Narrow feedback license to non-content telemetry + aggregated signals only; put model retrain into an explicit opt-in annex with pricing.
- Option C (conservative): Remove feedback license entirely; offer paid program for training access.

Action items:
- Laura, can you draft a short paragraph that limits "Feedback" to anonymized, aggregated signals and disallows use for model retraining or commercialized derivative products? Also include whether the license should survive termination.
- Jordan, please confirm what Ops needs to implement an opt-in annex (timeline, data handling).

We should aim to get a mark from Kazi/legal by tomorrow EOD. Novaforge timeline: they want to avoid schedule slips for the PO.

Thanks — Alex

Alex/Jordan — thanks for the context and Sam's notes. Drafted a short compromise paragraph and attached suggested wording (MSA_IP_Suggested_Wording.docx). Key points I put forward: 

- Customer Output: explicit language that "Customer retains ownership of output generated by the Service."
- Feedback License (narrow): "Customer hereby grants Redwood a perpetual, non-exclusive, royalty-free, worldwide license to use Customer Feedback solely to improve the performance, reliability and quality of Redwood's services and internal tooling. 'Customer Feedback' expressly excludes Customer Confidential Information and PII and may not be used for external commercialization or sold as a derivative product."
- Training / Model Retrain (opt-in): "Redwood shall not use Customer Content for model training or to create derivative models without Customer's explicit opt-in via an annex to the Order Form. Any such opt-in will be subject to separate commercial terms and additional data handling safeguards."
- Telemetry: allow collection of non-content telemetry by default; content-based telemetry only under opt-in and subject to masking/aggregation examples (I added two example sanitization steps in the doc).
- Survival: feedback license survives termination to permit continued internal analysis of anonymized feedback collected during the term; propose a 3-year usage window post-termination limited to aggregate metrics (happy to shorten if Novaforge insists).

I'll flag two negotiation levers for the call: survival window (3 yrs vs no survival) and whether "improve services" language is sufficient vs Novaforge's ask to ban model retrain in any form. If Novaforge wants a total ban on training, we should offer Option B above (training only via paid annex).

Next steps I recommend: (1) Alex send Laura's paragraph back to Sam as a one-paragraph compromise; (2) if Novaforge accepts in principle, route to Karthik/legal for a final quick sign-off; (3) include opt-in annex draft for training (Jordan to confirm ops feasibility).

Attached: MSA_IP_Suggested_Wording.docx 

Laura Bennett
Head of Contracts, Redwood Inference
